pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

pages.title: Logic pulser/probe digital signal tracing and fault isolation
pages.text: Digital signal tracing follows expected logic states and transitions through a known path. A logic probe observes HIGH, LOW and often pulse/activity; a logic pulser can provide a controlled transition to a safe node. First verify power, ground/reference and logic-family thresholds. Then choose a known stimulus and predict the state at each boundary. If an upstream node never changes, the fault may be before that point; if a safe forced pulse reaches an input but no expected downstream transition appears, the downstream gate/enable/output path becomes suspect. Oscilloscopes or logic analyzers are preferred when pulse width/timing/order matters. Do not pulse bidirectional buses, analog nodes or outputs actively driven against the pulser without confirming the tool/circuit permits it. The objective is to isolate the first incorrect logic relationship, not simply to find a pin that “looks dead.”
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

pages.title: Ports connect digital logic to physical pins through configuration
pages.text: A GPIO peripheral typically includes mode/direction, output data, input data, pull-up/down, drive/speed, and alternate-function controls. The physical pin can be multiplexed among GPIO and peripherals. Setting an output register does not prove the package pin changed if the port clock is disabled, the pin is in alternate/analog mode, the board routes it elsewhere, or an external circuit forces the node. Conversely, the input register can report the physical level even when output intent differs. This distinction becomes central to embedded debugging.
pages.sourceLesson: Bit fields, ports, processors, and stored state

pages.title: Sequential logic remembers state
pages.text: Combinational output depends on current inputs. Latches, flip-flops, counters, and registers include stored state, often updated by a clock or control edge. Setup and hold constraints say data must be stable around the sampling edge. Asynchronous set/reset can override normal clocked behavior. This introduces time into digital reasoning: the same input may yield different output because the previous state differs.
pages.remember: For sequential logic, always write current state, input/event, and next state.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

pages.title: Sequential logic adds memory and timing
pages.text: Combinational output depends only on present inputs. Sequential circuits also depend on stored state. Latches and flip-flops store bits; registers group storage; counters step through states; clocks coordinate updates. Setup and hold times define windows around a sampling edge during which input must be stable. Asynchronous set/reset inputs can override normal clocked operation. This timing perspective matters because a truth table alone cannot explain why a circuit sometimes captures the wrong state or misses a short pulse.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

pages.title: Counters, buses, clocks, timing, and logic families
pages.text: A counter advances through a defined state sequence in response to clock events; ripple counters propagate changes stage-to-stage, while synchronous counters update stages from a common clock. A bus is a shared set of conductors/signals carrying data, address or control information among functional blocks; bus direction, width, enable/tri-state behavior and timing must be understood before probing. Digital clocks establish event timing. Frequency and period describe rate, while propagation delay, rise/fall time, jitter, skew, setup and hold describe whether data is valid when sampled. Logic families such as TTL and CMOS have defined supply ranges and HIGH/LOW input/output thresholds; a voltage between guaranteed LOW and HIGH regions is not a valid state. CMOS inputs must not float, and 5 V TTL/CMOS outputs are not automatically safe for 3.3 V MCU inputs.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

pages.title: A logical 1 is a voltage range, not the word “high”
pages.text: Digital families specify input-low maximum, input-high minimum, and output guarantees. Voltages in the undefined region may produce unpredictable interpretation. Noise margin is the distance between guaranteed output and required input thresholds. Never assume 5 V logic is safe for a 3.3 V input; verify absolute maximum and input specifications. A DMM may show an average that hides fast transitions.
pages.remember: Translate logic claims into voltage thresholds and timing conditions.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

pages.title: Unconnected inputs do not have a reliable state
pages.text: A floating CMOS input can respond to leakage, capacitance, and noise. Pull-up or pull-down resistors define a default while allowing another device/switch to override it. Open-drain/open-collector outputs actively pull one direction and rely on a shared pull resistor for the other. Choose pull value by current, speed, leakage, and bus capacitance—not habit alone.
pages.remember: Every digital input needs a defined state in every operating condition.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

pages.title: Mechanical switches create multiple transitions
pages.text: Contacts bounce for a short interval, so one press can be sampled as many edges. Hardware RC/Schmitt filtering or software time/state logic can debounce it. A long blocking delay may hide bounce but also blocks other work. Verify with a scope/logic analyzer and test press/release behavior, not only one successful count.
pages.remember: The truth table may be perfect while the time-domain signal violates the assumption of one clean edge.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

pages.title: Debounce is a time-domain problem
pages.text: Mechanical switches physically bounce, producing multiple transitions over milliseconds. A DMM may show only an average or stable final state and miss the bounce completely. Debounce can be done with RC/Schmitt hardware, firmware timing/state logic, or both. The design should define a minimum stable interval or acceptance rule rather than insert an arbitrary delay with no understanding of consequences. A logic analyzer or scope shows the raw event and makes the debounce strategy testable.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

detail.problem: A pushbutton input uses a 10 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V and shorts to ground when pressed. The input capacitance plus wiring is approximated as 100 pF. Estimate RC rise time scale after release and explain why real mechanical bounce is still much slower.
steps: The electrical pull-up edge from simple capacitance settles in a few microseconds.
Mechanical bounce can last milliseconds, thousands of times longer.
Therefore the pull-up alone defines the idle state but does not necessarily debounce the mechanical contact.
detail.answer: RC time scale is about 1 us; mechanical bounce remains a separate millisecond-scale phenomenon.
detail.meaning: Do not confuse electrical edge shaping from capacitance with actual mechanical contact bounce.

Verify every unselected bit matches the original.

Explain the difference between a Boolean HIGH and a guaranteed electrical HIGH. Then explain why a pull-up is needed on an open-drain or switch input and how you would prove debounce works with an instrument.

questions.prompt: What is the output of a two-input AND gate for inputs 1 and 0?
questions.explanation: AND is high only when all inputs are high.

questions.prompt: What is the output of a two-input XOR gate for inputs 1 and 1?
choices: A stored copy of the previous input
questions.explanation: XOR is high for unequal input bits and low when they match.

questions.prompt: For an active-high NOR SR latch, S = 1 and R = 0 requests which state?
questions.explanation: The NOR SR latch is set by S high with R low. This convention differs from an active-low NAND latch; see the book errata.

questions.prompt: A binary counter has four flip-flops. How many distinct bit patterns can it represent?
questions.explanation: Four binary bits give 2⁴ = 16 possible states, normally 0 through 15 in an unsigned count.

questions.prompt: What must be compared before connecting outputs and inputs from different logic families?
choices: Guaranteed output levels, input thresholds and allowed voltages
Only the number of gates on a chip
Only whether both use binary symbols
questions.explanation: Binary names do not guarantee electrical compatibility. Datasheet limits control interfacing.

course.title: Digital testing and signal fault isolation
course.prerequisites: Logic probe/pulser, digital scope, counter, high/low, floating and timing faults
course.misconceptions: A floating pin is valid low; all digital inputs tolerate same voltage

sections.title: Digital probes, pulsers and logic measurement
sections.teachingSpecification: Define prerequisites; teach concept physically and quantitatively; demonstrate a reasoned worked example with labeled visual and units when applicable.

sections.title: Digital-signal troubleshooting and fault isolation
sections.teachingSpecification: Define prerequisites; teach concept physically and quantitatively; demonstrate a reasoned worked example with labeled visual and units when applicable.

objectives.title: List the uses and precautions for logic test probes
Explain how logic pulsers are used
Distinguish how pulsers are used for digital signal tracing
Describe how logic probes are used to verify states in digital equipment
Explain how to troubleshoot digital signals

pages.title: Build a fault model before probing
pages.text: Write the expected behavior and measured symptom under exact conditions. List a few plausible causes across power, connection, component, configuration, firmware, and instrument setup. Rank by evidence and consequence, not familiarity. A test is strong when different hypotheses predict different outcomes.
pages.remember: If every possible result leads to the same next action, the test did not discriminate.
pages.sourceLesson: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

pages.title: Fault isolation follows layers
pages.text: No edges means peripheral/MCU pin configuration or software path may be absent. Correct edges but no ACK suggests address, power, level, pull-up, reset, or device presence for I2C. Correct SPI clock/MOSI with wrong MISO can indicate mode, chip-select, wiring, device state, or bus contention. A decoder saying 'NACK' is not enough; inspect raw levels/rise time and device power. After a fix, repeat the exact transaction and one boundary case such as disconnected device or invalid register.
pages.sourceLesson: Datasheet-to-wire integration and bus fault isolation

pages.title: Choose the instrument from the question
pages.text: Use a DMM for accurate steady values, continuity, and resistance; use a scope when time behavior, ripple, noise, edge shape, or intermittent change matters; use the supply display as a quick current-consumption clue, not as the only measurement. Ask what quantity and time scale distinguish your hypotheses. A stable 3.3 V DMM reading does not prove a clock is running, while a scope trace may miss a very slow average drift better captured by logging.
pages.remember: Question → expected signal → required bandwidth/resolution → safest instrument and connection.
pages.sourceLesson: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty

pages.title: Write the question before choosing the probe
pages.text: A professional measurement begins with a decision question such as 'Is the 3.3 V rail collapsing during radio transmit?' or 'Does the MCU pin actually toggle after the register is set?' From that question, define the quantity, expected range, reference, instrument, connection, bandwidth/time resolution, and stop condition. Without the question, it is easy to collect screenshots that look technical but do not distinguish any cause. A good plan predicts what each hypothesis would produce before measurement, which turns the instrument into a reasoning tool rather than a camera.
pages.sourceLesson: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty

pages.title: High-information tests reduce the search space
pages.text: A test is valuable when its outcomes split the remaining hypotheses. Measuring a point that all causes predict will be normal adds confidence but little discrimination. Divide-and-conquer chooses a boundary near the middle of the functional path. Known-good substitution is powerful when the substitute is actually compatible and controlled. Signal tracing follows a known stimulus. Rail-by-rail checks separate power domains. The method is selected because it addresses the structure of the fault, not because it is a favorite instrument.
pages.sourceLesson: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

pages.title: I²C shares two open-drain lines
pages.text: A controller initiates START, sends an address plus direction, transfers bytes with ACK/NACK, and ends or repeats with STOP/START. SDA carries data; SCL carries clock. Devices pull lines low while resistors return them high, allowing wired sharing. Address notation can be 7-bit or shifted 8-bit in some documents; confirm API expectation. Rise time depends on pull-up resistance and bus capacitance.
pages.remember: Idle high, START/STOP, address/direction, ACK/NACK, bytes—and a pull-up path.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: SPI trades more wires for direct full-duplex shifting
pages.text: A controller provides clock and selects a peripheral with chip select; MOSI and MISO carry opposite directions. CPOL and CPHA define clock idle level and sampling/shift edges; both sides must use the same mode. Word length, bit order, maximum clock, and chip-select timing come from the datasheet. There is no universal acknowledgment, so plausible-looking wrong data is possible.
pages.remember: For SPI, capture clock, chip select, and both data directions together.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: A decoder is an assistant, not an oracle
pages.text: Set analyzer reference/ground, input threshold, sample rate comfortably above signal bandwidth, correct channel mapping, and protocol parameters. Inspect analog shape with a scope when rise time or voltage is suspect. Compare decoded transaction with raw edges and datasheet sequence. A decoder can label wrong data neatly when mode/address/settings are wrong.
pages.remember: Validate capture setup and raw timing before believing protocol labels.
pages.sourceLesson: Datasheet-to-wire integration and bus fault isolation

pages.title: Bus symptoms map to different layers
pages.text: Lines stuck low suggest shorts, unpowered devices/back-powering, or a device holding the bus. No activity suggests pin mux, clock enable, driver path, or trigger/capture setup. Address NACK suggests address, wiring, power, pull-ups, or timing. ACK with wrong data suggests register sequence, byte order, mode, or scaling. Intermittent errors with speed/length suggest rise time, signal integrity, grounding, or timing margin.
pages.remember: Name the layer—electrical, configuration, transaction, interpretation, or application—before changing code.
pages.sourceLesson: Datasheet-to-wire integration and bus fault isolation

pages.title: Signal levels, connectors, grounding, mismatch, and conflict symptoms
pages.text: Interfaces fail when two devices disagree about voltage range, current drive, reference/ground, impedance, polarity, timing, connector pinout or signaling convention. Before connecting equipment, identify each side’s output type and allowable input range from documentation. A connector is not just a shape: keying, pin numbering, contact rating, shielding, retention and intended signal/power class matter. Grounds may be chassis, protective earth, analog reference, digital return or isolated secondary; tying them together blindly can create loops, shorts or unsafe paths, while failing to share a required signal reference can make a logic link unreadable. Power-source mismatch may present as no operation, overheating, reset, blown protection or damage. Signal-level conflict may produce clipping, constant logic HIGH/LOW, intermittent data, excessive noise, hum, distorted analog output, bus contention or damaged I/O. Level shifting, buffering, isolation, impedance matching or correct cabling solves specific incompatibilities; an adapter that only changes connector shape may solve none of them.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: Interfaces are electrical plus protocol contracts
pages.text: Before connecting devices, define voltage levels, reference/ground, direction, output type, input thresholds, source/sink current, impedance/loading, connector pinout, timing, and protocol. A connector that physically fits can still carry incompatible voltage or signal type. Logic-level UART, RS-232, USB, I2C, SPI, analog voltage, current loop, and differential buses are different contracts. Level shifters, buffers, isolation, termination, or transceivers are selected to solve a specific mismatch rather than added generically.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: SPI uses dedicated clock/data and explicit chip selection
pages.text: SPI commonly uses SCLK, MOSI, MISO, and one chip-select line per device or another selection scheme. Unlike I2C, outputs are generally actively driven and there is no built-in addressing or ACK. Clock polarity (CPOL) and phase (CPHA) define when data changes and is sampled. Wrong mode can produce shifted or corrupted data even when frequency and wiring are correct. MISO bus sharing requires inactive devices to release the line; chip-select timing and voltage levels must be checked from the datasheet.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

examples.title: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty

detail.problem: A 100 mV ripple rides on a 5 V rail. The scope trace is off-screen at a sensitive vertical scale.
steps: Keep the ground clip on the approved circuit reference.
Start in DC coupling to confirm the 5 V level and safe signal range.
Use vertical position/offset or then AC coupling to examine the small ripple.
Enable an appropriate bandwidth limit if high-frequency noise is not the question.
Record that AC coupling removed the DC component; do not report the trace as absolute rail voltage.
detail.answer: Verify the DC level first, then isolate ripple with documented coupling and scale.
detail.transfer: This same sequence is used to characterize regulator ripple without losing the fact that a DC rail is present.

examples.title: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty

detail.problem: A UART line should idle at 3.3 V and transmit bursts every second. A scope capture shows 2.1 V average with no obvious transitions.
steps: The word 'average' suggests the measurement may not be configured to reveal digital timing.
Verify the probe reference, attenuation, DC coupling, and vertical scale.
Set a time base that can show the 1 s burst interval or use single/normal trigger on an edge; then zoom into the bit timing.
If the line still sits near 2.1 V, investigate contention, wrong voltage domain, heavy loading, or incorrect pull network.
detail.answer: First prove the measurement setup can reveal the expected idle level and transitions, then treat a persistent 2.1 V level as an electrical fault symptom.
detail.meaning: A measurement plan separates 'the signal is wrong' from 'the observation method cannot show the signal.'

examples.title: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

detail.problem: A sensor returns no data. Its VDD is 0 V, upstream regulator output is 3.3 V, and continuity from regulator to connector is open.
steps: Firmware/protocol cannot work without sensor power.
The regulator is operating, so isolate the interconnect between rail and sensor connector.
Inspect fuse/link/trace/connector orientation and test continuity with power off.
Repair the confirmed open, then verify VDD and protocol response.
detail.answer: The evidence isolates an open power path upstream of the sensor.
detail.transfer: One causal chain avoids wasting time changing addresses or code before power exists.

examples.title: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

detail.problem: A sensor reads correctly over I2C until a motor is enabled, then NACKs occur. Hypotheses: supply noise, SDA/SCL electrical edge degradation, or firmware scheduling delay.
steps: Capture sensor rail and I2C lines during motor enable while logging firmware timing/error counters.
If rail dips below sensor limits at the exact NACK, supply integrity is supported.
If rail is stable but edges slow/ring or violate thresholds, electrical bus loading/noise is stronger.
If electrical signals are valid but transactions begin too late or timeout in software, scheduling/firmware becomes stronger.
detail.answer: Use synchronized electrical and software evidence so one event can separate power, signal-integrity, and firmware timing causes.
detail.meaning: A high-information test is designed around how candidate causes would look different.

examples.title: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

detail.problem: A 12-bit ADC with 3.3 V reference reports code 2048 on a 0–4095 scale. Estimate voltage.
steps: Voltage ≈ fraction × 3.3 V ≈ 1.65 V.
State the assumed code range/reference and expected quantization.
Compare with an independent meter measurement if available.
detail.answer: Approximately 1.65 V.
detail.transfer: A correct formula with the wrong reference or alignment still yields a believable wrong result.

guided.text: Write a measurement-plan row for checking a 3.3 V rail during MCU reset: quantity, expected range, instrument, connection, time resolution, and stop condition.
A meter reads 4.998 V three times on a nominal 5 V rail. Explain what you can and cannot claim without the meter accuracy specification and system tolerance.
For a suspected 20 us glitch, explain why a DMM may miss the event and choose scope settings that would make the event observable.
Rewrite three vague hypotheses into testable statements with predicted observations.
For a four-stage signal chain, choose a half-split measurement and explain what each possible result tells you about the remaining search space.
Given one intermittent failure, state how you would preserve configuration, trigger/capture evidence, and avoid changing multiple variables before reproduction.

teachBack: Explain how you turn a troubleshooting question into a reproducible measurement plan. Distinguish accuracy, resolution, repeatability, and loading using one real instrument example.

Take a no-output or bus-failure example and teach how to create three competing hypotheses, select one high-information test, interpret each possible outcome, and avoid confusing symptom with root cause.
Compare UART, I2C, and SPI electrically and logically. Then explain one I2C rise-time failure and one SPI CPOL/CPHA failure using what you would expect to see on a scope or logic analyzer.

Choose an I2C or SPI device and teach the path from datasheet pin/timing requirements to wiring, MCU configuration, first transaction, analyzer capture, register interpretation, and one layered fault diagnosis.

questions.prompt: What makes a scope screenshot reproducible evidence?
choices: The measured value plus test point, reference, probe/coupling/timebase/scale, and expected behavior
A phone photo with no labels
questions.explanation: Correct. Context and settings let another person reconstruct and judge the measurement.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a defensible root cause?
choices: An open connector pin removed sensor VDD; continuity and voltage evidence identified it, and repair restored both rail and data
questions.explanation: Correct. It names the mechanism, evidence, correction, and verified effect.

questions.prompt: What creates the high level on a standard I²C bus?
choices: Pull-up resistors return released open-drain lines high
questions.explanation: Correct. Devices actively pull low and release; pull-ups establish high.

questions.prompt: The analyzer decodes no I²C traffic and both lines remain low. What should be checked first?
choices: Electrical power, shorts, pull-ups, and whether a device is holding the lines
questions.explanation: Correct. A physically stuck bus must be resolved before transaction parsing.

course.misconceptions: Any identical connector means compatible; ground reference never matters

objectives.title: List input circuit signal levels which may be expected for various common electronics products or test equipment
Explain the purposes of plugs and connectors and why it is necessary to use the proper ones per application
Explain grounding, proper and improper methods, and the results of power source mismatch
List potential signal conflict symptoms
Describe other electronic interfacing such as USB, Zigbee, I2C (inter-integrated circuit)

pages.title: USB, I2C, and Zigbee interfaces
pages.text: USB, I2C and Zigbee solve very different interface problems. USB is a host/device serial bus with differential data signaling, defined connectors/power roles and enumeration: a device must be electrically connected and then recognized/configured by the host protocol stack. I2C is a short-distance board-level two-wire bus using SDA and SCL with open-drain/open-collector style drivers and pull-up resistors; devices use addresses and acknowledge (ACK/NACK) transfers. The bus can fail from wrong address, missing/incorrect pull-ups, voltage-level mismatch, stuck-low device, timing or wiring faults. Zigbee is a low-power wireless networking technology built on IEEE 802.15.4 radios and adds network/application behavior beyond a simple point-to-point wire. It introduces channel/interference, joining/addressing/network topology and RF-range considerations. “Serial interface” is therefore not enough detail: physical/electrical layer and protocol behavior must both be identified.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: Interfaces are electrical plus protocol contracts
pages.text: Before connecting devices, define voltage levels, reference/ground, direction, output type, input thresholds, source/sink current, impedance/loading, connector pinout, timing, and protocol. Logic-level UART, RS-232, USB, I2C, SPI, analog voltage, current loop, and differential buses are different contracts. Level shifters, buffers, isolation, termination, or transceivers are selected to solve a specific mismatch rather than added generically.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: Signal levels, connectors, grounding, mismatch, and conflict symptoms
pages.text: Interfaces fail when two devices disagree about voltage range, current drive, reference/ground, impedance, polarity, timing, connector pinout or signaling convention. Before connecting equipment, identify each side’s output type and allowable input range from documentation. Grounds may be chassis, protective earth, analog reference, digital return or isolated secondary; tying them together blindly can create loops, shorts or unsafe paths, while failing to share a required signal reference can make a logic link unreadable. Power-source mismatch may present as no operation, overheating, reset, blown protection or damage. Level shifting, buffering, isolation, impedance matching or correct cabling solves specific incompatibilities; an adapter that only changes connector shape may solve none of them.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: Interfacing, distortion, conflicts, fault isolation, and signal levels
pages.text: Interfacing alarm/security, entertainment and information products requires compatible signal type, level, reference, impedance and connector/protocol. Audio levels are relative categories rather than one exact voltage: microphone level is small, line level is larger but intended for high-impedance line inputs, headphone outputs can drive moderate loads, and speaker outputs deliver far greater current/power to low-impedance loads. Connecting a speaker-level output to a microphone input can clip or damage the input. Distortion can come from clipping/overload, crossover/nonlinearity, bad source material, speaker excursion/thermal limit, grounding/hum, bandwidth limitation or sampling/codec artifacts. To isolate a glitch between discrete units, substitute a known-good source/load/cable or observe the signal at the interface while changing one element. Ground loops may create hum; incompatible formats or levels may create silence, clipping, noise or intermittent behavior.
pages.sourceLesson: Media, connectors, signal paths, and optical fundamentals

pages.title: Electrical UART is not the same thing as RS-232 or USB
pages.text: MCU UART pins usually use logic-level voltages referenced to board ground. Traditional RS-232 uses different voltage levels and polarity conventions and requires a transceiver; USB is a completely different differential protocol. A USB-to-UART adapter contains conversion logic and must be set to a compatible logic voltage. TX and RX are directional: one device's TX normally connects to the other's RX, and a common reference is required unless the interface is isolated/differential through suitable hardware.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: I2C uses shared open-drain lines and addressing
pages.text: I2C commonly uses SDA and SCL with open-drain/open-collector behavior and pull-up resistors. Devices pull lines low and release them for high; no device should actively drive high in the usual arrangement. A START condition occurs when SDA falls while SCL is high; STOP when SDA rises while SCL is high. Address and R/W information is followed by ACK/NACK bits and data bytes. Pull-up value, bus capacitance, voltage domain, address conflicts, clock stretching, and rise time affect operation. A missing ACK is a symptom, not a complete diagnosis.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: SPI trades more wires for direct full-duplex shifting
pages.text: A controller provides clock and selects a peripheral with chip select; MOSI and MISO carry opposite directions. CPOL and CPHA define clock idle level and sampling/shift edges; both sides must use the same mode. Word length, bit order, maximum clock, and chip-select timing come from the datasheet. There is no universal acknowledgment, so plausible-looking wrong data is possible.
pages.remember: For SPI, capture clock, chip select, and both data directions together.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: SPI uses dedicated clock/data and explicit chip selection
pages.text: SPI commonly uses SCLK, MOSI, MISO, and one chip-select line per device or another selection scheme. Unlike I2C, outputs are generally actively driven and there is no built-in addressing or ACK. Clock polarity (CPOL) and phase (CPHA) define when data changes and is sampled. Wrong mode can produce shifted or corrupted data even when frequency and wiring are correct. MISO bus sharing requires inactive devices to release the line; chip-select timing and voltage levels must be checked from the datasheet.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

pages.title: TX crosses to RX and both ends need a reference
pages.text: Device TX connects to host RX, device RX to host TX, with common ground/reference for single-ended logic UART. Do not connect two outputs together. Logic-level UART is not automatically RS-232; RS-232 uses different voltages/polarity and requires a transceiver. Confirm 3.3 V/5 V tolerance before connection.
pages.remember: Protocol name does not guarantee electrical compatibility.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: Garbled data is a useful symptom
pages.text: Consistently wrong characters often suggest baud/clock/format mismatch. Nothing at the MCU TX pin suggests firmware/pin-mux/clock path; correct MCU waveform but nothing at the adapter suggests wiring or level conversion; correct bytes in a terminal but not Python suggests port/encoding/line-handling software. A logic analyzer or scope localizes the boundary.
pages.remember: Observe the signal at each interface before rewriting both ends.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: Errors point to different layers
pages.text: No transitions can mean wrong pin, no firmware output, broken wire, missing ground, or wrong measurement point. Repeating but unreadable patterns can mean wrong baud/framing or voltage-level mismatch. Clean electrical frames with wrong characters can indicate framing/encoding assumptions. Correct bytes reaching the host but wrong application values point to parsing/protocol logic. A logic analyzer decoder is useful only after the raw waveform levels and timing make sense; a decoder setting can hide the real problem by confidently interpreting the wrong baud.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: Choose media from signal, environment, and termination
pages.text: Conductors have resistance, capacitance, inductance, shielding, impedance, bandwidth, and mechanical limits. Coax controls geometry/impedance and shielding; twisted pair improves rejection of common interference; ribbon/harness wiring emphasizes organized point-to-point connection. Connector family is not enough—keying, pinout, gender, impedance, rating, strain relief, and termination quality matter.
pages.remember: Signal type + impedance/bandwidth + environment + connector/pinout + workmanship.
pages.sourceLesson: Media, connectors, signal paths, and optical fundamentals

pages.title: Audio and video systems are source–processing–path–load chains
pages.text: Audio stages may include transducer, preamplifier, filtering, power amplifier, cable, and speaker. Video adds timing/bandwidth and format conversion. A fault at one boundary affects everything downstream. Hum/noise, attenuation, clipping, loss of one channel, and sync/display symptoms suggest different locations. Match impedance/level conventions and avoid assuming connector shape defines the signal.
pages.remember: Trace direction and expected level at each block boundary.
pages.sourceLesson: Media, connectors, signal paths, and optical fundamentals

pages.title: Wire construction, gauge, and identification
pages.text: Wire and cable differ by conductor material, solid/stranded construction, insulation/jacket, shielding, twist and intended environment. Stranded wire tolerates flexing better; solid conductors hold shape and are common in fixed wiring/board work. American Wire Gauge is inverse: a smaller AWG number means a larger conductor diameter/cross-section and generally lower resistance/higher current capacity when installation conditions are comparable. Gauge selection also depends on insulation temperature, bundle/ambient conditions, length/voltage drop, connector limits and code/application requirements. Communications cable identification includes pair/category and pinout conventions; UTP uses twisted pairs to improve balanced-noise rejection, while shielded cable adds a conductive screen that must be terminated/bonded according to the system design. Never infer allowable current from gauge alone without the governing application.

examples.title: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

detail.problem: A 12-bit ADC with 3.3 V reference reports code 2048 on a 0–4095 scale. Estimate voltage.
steps: Voltage ≈ fraction × 3.3 V ≈ 1.65 V.
State the assumed code range/reference and expected quantization.
Compare with an independent meter measurement if available.
detail.answer: Approximately 1.65 V.
detail.transfer: A correct formula with the wrong reference or alignment still yields a believable wrong result.

examples.title: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

detail.problem: An I2C bus at 3.3 V has 10 kOhm pull-ups and about 400 pF capacitance. Rise time is too slow at the target speed.
steps: Open-drain devices rely on RC charging through pull-ups for the rising edge.
Approximate time constant is R*C=10,000*400e-12=4 us, already too large for many faster I2C timing requirements.
A lower pull-up resistance can improve rise time but increases low-state sink current.
Choose pull-ups from bus capacitance, timing requirement, device sink-current limits, and voltage domain rather than copying one value.
detail.answer: The 10 kOhm pull-up is too weak for the stated capacitance/speed; reduce resistance within sink-current/timing limits.
detail.meaning: I2C is a protocol and an analog RC electrical network at the same time.

examples.title: Media, connectors, signal paths, and optical fundamentals

detail.problem: An optical link has +0 dBm launch power, 8 dB path loss, and receiver sensitivity −10 dBm.
steps: Received power = 0 dBm − 8 dB = −8 dBm.
Margin relative to −10 dBm sensitivity is 2 dB.
Positive margin predicts possible operation, but 2 dB may be poor allowance for aging/temperature/contamination.
Check specified design margin and connector cleanliness/measurement uncertainty.
detail.answer: Predicted −8 dBm with 2 dB margin.
detail.transfer: dB path budgets use addition/subtraction even though underlying power ratios multiply.

examples.title: Media, connectors, signal paths, and optical fundamentals

detail.problem: A 50 ohm RF source is connected through a 75 ohm coax segment and adapters to a 50 ohm load. The system shows reflections.
steps: The physical connection may have continuity, but characteristic-impedance mismatches exist at 50-to-75 and 75-to-50 ohm transitions.
At sufficiently high frequency/fast edge, part of the wave reflects at each discontinuity.
A DMM continuity test cannot characterize this reflection behavior.
Use the correct impedance cable/connectors or characterize with appropriate RF/TDR methods; compare with a known matched load.
detail.answer: The fault is signal-integrity mismatch, not simple DC continuity.
detail.meaning: Media and connector selection must match the signal's frequency/impedance requirements.

examples.title: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

detail.problem: At 115200 baud, estimate one bit time and a 10-bit 8N1 character time.
steps: 8N1 commonly has 1 start + 8 data + 1 stop = 10 bits.
Tchar ≈ 86.8 µs.
Maximum ideal character rate is about 11,520 per second before software/protocol overhead.
detail.answer: About 8.68 µs per bit and 86.8 µs per 8N1 character.
detail.transfer: A logic-analyzer cursor can verify baud by measuring bit width.

guided.text: Draw a START, 7-bit address, R/W, ACK, one data byte, ACK, STOP I2C transaction and label who drives/releases SDA.

teachBack: Compare UART, I2C, and SPI electrically and logically. Then explain one I2C rise-time failure and one SPI CPOL/CPHA failure using what you would expect to see on a scope or logic analyzer.

Teach the differences among copper/coax/fiber media and among LED/LCD/OLED/photo devices. Then explain why continuity is only one kind of evidence and what instrument you would choose for a high-frequency or optical fault.
Explain an 8N1 UART frame from idle through stop bit, calculate bit time from baud, and describe how you would distinguish wrong baud from wrong voltage/wiring using raw waveform evidence.

questions.prompt: In ordinary I²C communication, which two signal lines are used?
questions.explanation: I²C uses serial data and serial clock. It also needs compatible levels and a suitable reference connection.

questions.prompt: Why does a conventional open-drain I²C bus need pull-up resistors?
choices: Devices pull low and release the line; pull-ups establish high levels.
Each device actively drives a high voltage at all times.
Pull-ups convert DC into radio waves.
Pull-ups remove the need for voltage compatibility.
questions.explanation: Pull-ups restore a released line high; their value and bus capacitance affect rise time.

questions.prompt: A 3.3 V microcontroller input is not rated for 5 V. What must be checked before attaching a 5 V output?
choices: A suitable level conversion or otherwise compatible interface
Only that the connectors physically fit
Only whether the signals have the same name
Whether both boards have green solder mask
questions.explanation: Logic levels and absolute maximum limits matter. A matching connector does not establish electrical compatibility.

questions.prompt: Two low-voltage, nonisolated UART devices need which reference relationship?
choices: A compatible common signal reference established safely
No reference connection under any conditions
A direct connection of every power rail together
An arbitrary mains-earth connection to a signal pin
questions.explanation: Nonisolated logic voltage is measured relative to a reference. Check the equipment grounding and power arrangement before joining devices.

questions.prompt: Two connectors fit together, but their pinouts differ. What does the fit establish?
choices: Mechanical compatibility only, not electrical compatibility
That all signal levels are safe
That each pin has the same function
That the equipment can be powered immediately
questions.explanation: Check pin assignments, voltages, current ratings and signal requirements before connection.

questions.prompt: What creates the high level on a standard I²C bus?
choices: Pull-up resistors return released open-drain lines high
questions.explanation: Correct. Devices actively pull low and release; pull-ups establish high.

questions.prompt: Which connection is correct for logic-level UART?
choices: TX to RX, RX to TX, and a verified common reference
Either line to mains earth only
questions.explanation: Correct. Data lines cross, reference is shared, and electrical compatibility must be verified.

objectives.title: Define microcontrollers and simple programming commands
Describe the major sections of a computer
Differentiate how the computer block diagram and flow charts are utilized

pages.title: A computer repeatedly moves, transforms, and stores information
pages.text: The CPU fetches instructions and data, decodes operations, executes them using registers/ALU, and updates state. RAM provides volatile working storage; flash/ROM retains code/data without power; peripherals connect timers, converters, communication, and pins; buses carry address, data, and control. A microcontroller integrates these blocks on one device.
pages.remember: CPU executes; memory stores; peripherals interact; buses connect.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: A computer is coordinated storage, processing, and I/O
pages.text: At a high level, a CPU fetches instructions and data from memory, executes operations using registers/ALU/control logic, and communicates with peripherals through buses or mapped interfaces. Volatile memory such as RAM loses contents without power; nonvolatile memory such as flash retains program/data. Storage, working memory, registers, cache, and peripheral registers serve different roles. A block diagram is useful because it shows where information is stored, transformed, and transferred without implying exact physical layout.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: An MCU is a computer plus tightly integrated peripherals
pages.text: A microcontroller combines a CPU core, nonvolatile program memory, RAM, clock/reset circuitry, buses, GPIO, timers, ADCs, communication peripherals, interrupt logic, and often debug hardware on one device. The CPU executes instructions, but most real embedded behavior depends on peripherals that run partly independently once configured. Memory maps assign address ranges to flash, RAM, system control, and peripheral registers. Reading a peripheral register at a documented address is therefore a hardware operation expressed through memory access.
pages.sourceLesson: MCU architecture, memory map, GPIO, and debug concepts

pages.title: Computer architecture, CPU blocks, memory, block diagrams, and flowcharts
pages.text: A computer system can be divided into input, processing, memory/storage, communication and output. Inside a processor/microprocessor, the control unit sequences operations, the arithmetic/logic unit performs calculations/logic, registers hold immediate working state, buses/interconnect move addresses/data/control, and clock/reset mechanisms coordinate startup/execution. Cache and memory interfaces reduce the speed gap to external memory. Volatile RAM loses contents without power; nonvolatile flash/ROM retains code/data; mass storage provides longer-term file storage with very different latency/endurance. A computer block diagram shows hardware/data relationships, while a software flowchart shows sequence and decisions. Troubleshooting uses both: “which block should receive this signal/data?” is a block-diagram question; “which branch should execute next?” is a flowchart question.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: PLC purpose, scan cycle, programming concepts, and languages
pages.text: A programmable logic controller is an industrial controller designed for deterministic I/O control and rugged environments. A basic PLC scan reads inputs, executes the control program, updates outputs and performs communications/diagnostics; exact behavior depends on platform. Ladder logic represents relay-like contacts/coils and is common in industrial work, while function-block, structured-text and other IEC-style languages express the same control intent in different forms. Programming concepts still include variables/tags, Boolean conditions, timers, counters, state, functions, sequence and error handling. Different languages exist because some make discrete control, math/data handling, state machines or reusable algorithms easier to express and maintain. A technician must distinguish a physical input state from a software tag and an output command from actual field voltage/current; forcing a software bit does not prove the field circuit is healthy.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: PLCs are computers optimized for industrial control
pages.text: A PLC reads inputs, executes a control program, updates outputs, and performs communications/diagnostics in a repeating scan or platform-specific execution model. Ladder logic uses relay-like contacts and coils; function block and structured text offer other representations. Timers, counters, state, interlocks, and fail-safe design connect software logic to physical I/O. A displayed software bit is not proof that a field voltage or actuator changed; technicians verify both program state and actual terminal behavior.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: Bits gain meaning from type and context
pages.text: The same pattern may represent an unsigned number, signed two’s-complement value, character, instruction, address, or flags. Width matters: an 8-bit unsigned value ranges 0–255; fixed-width C types make hardware intent explicit. Endianness determines byte order in multi-byte data, while bit numbering usually labels least-significant bit as bit 0. Never interpret raw memory without type, width, and byte order.
pages.remember: Bits do not label themselves; representation rules give them meaning.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: Source code passes through tools before hardware can execute it
pages.text: The preprocessor handles directives/macros/includes; the compiler translates C and diagnoses language issues; assembler produces machine-object code; linker resolves symbols and lays out sections into an executable/firmware image; loader/programmer places it into memory. Warnings are evidence about risk. A successful build proves syntax/tool completion, not correct behavior.
pages.remember: Build success, run success, and requirement success are three different gates.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: Peripherals and interface devices/cards
pages.text: A peripheral is an attached device that extends input, output, storage, sensing or communication capability: keyboards, displays, printers, drives, cameras, USB devices and network adapters are examples. Interface devices/chips/cards bridge electrical/protocol expectations between the CPU/system bus and external equipment. Examples include USB controllers/hubs, UART/serial interfaces, Ethernet/network interface controllers, storage controllers, audio codecs/interfaces, GPIO/I/O expanders and data-acquisition cards. Installing hardware is only part of bring-up: power, connector/pinout, bus enumeration, driver, address/resource configuration and functional test must all agree. An unrecognized peripheral may be a cable/power/port problem, missing driver, unsupported protocol/device class, resource/configuration issue or failed hardware.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: Source code becomes executable through stages
pages.text: C source files are preprocessed and compiled into object code; the linker combines objects/libraries and resolves symbols into an executable image; the image is loaded or programmed into memory and then executed. A syntax/type error is a compile-stage problem. An 'undefined reference' is commonly a link-stage problem. A program that builds but crashes is a runtime problem. Keeping those stages separate prevents random editing and becomes essential in embedded toolchains where startup code, linker scripts, flash layout, and programmer/debugger are additional boundaries.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: Ports and registers connect code to hardware
pages.text: A CPU accesses memory-mapped control/status locations to configure direction, function, timing, or data. Some bits are read-only, write-one-to-clear, self-clearing, or reserved. A microcontroller integrates CPU, memory, and peripherals; a microprocessor often depends on more external components. Ports provide groups of digital I/O, but pin multiplexing may assign alternate peripheral functions.
pages.remember: A register is an interface contract, not ordinary RAM.
pages.sourceLesson: Bit fields, ports, processors, and stored state

pages.title: Ports connect digital logic to physical pins through configuration
pages.text: A GPIO peripheral typically includes mode/direction, output data, input data, pull-up/down, drive/speed, and alternate-function controls. The physical pin can be multiplexed among GPIO and peripherals. Setting an output register does not prove the package pin changed if the port clock is disabled, the pin is in alternate/analog mode, the board routes it elsewhere, or an external circuit forces the node. Conversely, the input register can report the physical level even when output intent differs. This distinction becomes central to embedded debugging.
pages.sourceLesson: Bit fields, ports, processors, and stored state

pages.title: Stored state lives at different layers
pages.text: CPU registers hold immediate working state; RAM stores volatile data; flash stores program/nonvolatile content; peripheral registers represent hardware configuration/state; external devices maintain their own registers; firmware variables may be cached or optimized. A debugger view shows one layer at a moment in time. When behavior disagrees with expectation, ask which layer is authoritative for the claim. Reading a C variable called `led_on` is not the same as reading the GPIO output register, and neither is the same as measuring the pin voltage.
pages.sourceLesson: Bit fields, ports, processors, and stored state

pages.title: An MCU is a system of clocked blocks
pages.text: The Cortex-M core executes instructions; flash stores firmware; SRAM holds working data; buses connect core, memory, and peripherals; clock sources/dividers determine operating rates; reset establishes a known starting state; peripheral registers configure GPIO, timers, converters, and communication. The exact STM32 family matters because memory maps, clocks, pins, and peripherals vary.
pages.remember: Always identify exact MCU/board before trusting a pin name or example project.
pages.sourceLesson: MCU architecture, memory map, GPIO, and debug concepts

examples.title: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

detail.problem: An 8-bit unsigned counter holding 255 is incremented once.
steps: Eight unsigned bits represent 0 through 255.
255 is binary 11111111.
Adding one produces 1 00000000; only eight stored bits remain.
The stored result wraps to 0 in unsigned arithmetic.
detail.answer: 0, due to modulo-256 unsigned wrap.
detail.transfer: A wrapped timer/counter can break comparisons unless rollover is handled intentionally.

examples.title: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

detail.problem: A small C program compiles each source file successfully but the final build reports 'undefined reference to read_sensor'.
steps: Compilation succeeded, so the syntax in the individual source files is acceptable enough to produce objects.
The undefined reference appears during linking because a required symbol declaration/call exists but the linker cannot find a matching definition in linked objects/libraries.
Check whether the implementation file is included in the build, symbol spelling/signature matches, and the correct library/object is linked.
Do not troubleshoot runtime sensor wiring until an executable image exists.
detail.answer: Treat this as a link-stage dependency/symbol problem, not a runtime hardware failure.
detail.meaning: Identifying the build stage narrows the search space before any code or hardware change.

examples.title: Bit fields, ports, processors, and stored state

detail.problem: Register value is 0b10100101. Set bit 3 and clear bit 5 without changing others.
steps: Clear mask: ~(1<<5); AND clears bit 5.
0b10101101 with bit 5 cleared becomes 0b10001101.
Verify every unselected bit matches the original.
detail.transfer: The same pattern configures GPIO fields while preserving unrelated pins.

examples.title: Bit fields, ports, processors, and stored state

detail.problem: A control register is 0xA4. You must set bits 1 and 0 while preserving all other bits. What value results?
steps: Mask for bits 1 and 0 is 0x03 = 0000 0011.
Set with OR: 0xA4 | 0x03 = 0xA7.
Other bits remain unchanged because OR with 0 leaves them as they were.
detail.answer: 0xA7.
detail.meaning: Bit masks let firmware change one field without rewriting unrelated configuration.

examples.title: MCU architecture, memory map, GPIO, and debug concepts

detail.problem: Firmware writes GPIO A pin 5 high, but the board LED stays off.
steps: Confirm the board LED is actually connected to PA5 and whether it is active-high or active-low.
Inspect clock enable, GPIO mode, output type, and output register in the debugger.
Measure the physical pin relative to board ground.
Separate firmware register state from board net/LED behavior.
detail.answer: No single observation is enough; trace configuration, pin, board connection, and polarity.
detail.transfer: This layered model prevents “code vs hardware” guessing during bring-up.

guided.text: Classify five failures as compile, link, load/program, or runtime: syntax error, undefined reference, programmer cannot connect, program hard-faults, missing header declaration warning.
Draw CPU, RAM, flash/nonvolatile storage, and peripheral I/O blocks. Trace what happens from power-up to executing an instruction that reads an input.
Explain a PLC scan using a start/stop input and motor output, then identify what field measurement is needed to prove the output actually energized.
Starting from 0x5A, set bit 7, clear bit 3, and test whether bit 1 is set. Show binary or hex masks.
Create a GPIO debugging chain from C variable -> peripheral register -> alternate function/mode -> package pin -> board net -> LED/load.
Explain when a read-modify-write operation could be dangerous on a status/control register and what documentation you would check.

teachBack: Explain the path from C source file to running executable, then connect that path to CPU, memory, and I/O hardware. Include how a PLC scan differs from assuming software state equals physical output.

Explain how a bit mask changes selected register bits without disturbing others, then trace a GPIO command from firmware variable to register to pin to physical load and name a failure possible at each layer.
Explain an MCU from CPU and memory out to a physical GPIO pin. Include clock/reset, memory-mapped registers, pin mux, board net, and what SWD can and cannot prove.
Compare UART, I2C, and SPI electrically and logically. Then explain one I2C rise-time failure and one SPI CPOL/CPHA failure using what you would expect to see on a scope or logic analyzer.

objectives.title: Explain knowledge of basic computer operation
Explain steps in installation/set up of a computer
Explain the reasons and choices used in configuring a computer
Describe proper loading and storage of common programs and applications
Explain basic common utilities software and list reasons for their use
List ways to backup data and the vital importance of doing so
Explain the causes of line surges and viruses and protection procedures against each
Explain how to access the Internet, cybersecurity best practices and common applications
Describe how to download a service or application, data or software
Explain the differences between an individual stand-alone computer and basic networking

pages.title: Basic operation, setup/configuration, and stand-alone versus networked computers
pages.text: A computer boots through firmware/bootloader stages into an operating system that manages CPU time, memory, files, devices and applications. Setup begins with verified hardware/power, firmware settings where necessary, storage/OS installation, device drivers, user/security configuration, updates and functional tests. Configuration means selecting settings appropriate to hardware and use—display/network/ports, storage, permissions, services, time, power and application options—not randomly changing defaults. Drivers translate OS requests into device-specific operations. A stand-alone computer can operate without network services; a networked computer additionally depends on interface configuration, link, IP addressing, local switching/routing, DNS/name resolution and remote services. Troubleshooting therefore identifies which layer fails instead of reinstalling everything.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: Program installation, utilities, backups, downloads, and recovery
pages.text: Programs should be obtained from trusted sources, checked for supported OS/hardware/version, installed with the least privilege necessary, and recorded so the configuration can be reproduced. Utilities include file/disk tools, task/process monitors, logs/event viewers, compression/archive tools, diagnostics, update tools and security scanners; each answers a specific maintenance question. Backup means keeping recoverable copies separate from the working data. Useful strategies combine versions and, where appropriate, local plus offline/off-site/cloud copies; synchronization alone is not a backup because deletion/corruption can synchronize too. Recovery is not proven until a restore is tested. Downloads should be verified by source, filename/version, digital signature or checksum when provided, and scanned/handled according to security policy. Store installers/configuration notes where licensing and policy allow so a system can be rebuilt.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: Surges versus malware and practical cybersecurity/network use
pages.text: A line surge is an electrical overvoltage/transient problem; malware/virus infection is a software/security problem. Surge protection uses properly selected protective devices, grounding/bonding and system design, while malware protection uses patching, least privilege, reputable endpoint protection, application/source control and backups. One does not protect against the other. Internet access requires a functioning network interface/link and an IP path through switches/routers; DNS translates names to addresses, while application protocols/services operate above that. Cybersecurity basics include unique strong credentials with MFA where available, updates, phishing awareness, least privilege, trusted software sources, protected secrets, secure Wi-Fi/VPN practices as required, backups and prompt reporting of suspected compromise. A technician should preserve logs/evidence and follow organization incident procedures rather than experimenting on a suspected compromised production system.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: Technician computing is about reproducible operation
pages.text: Know how to install or load approved software from trusted sources, verify compatibility/version, use common utilities, preserve backups, and recover configurations. A downloaded tool should have a recorded source/version and, where provided, integrity/signature checks. Backups are not the same as synchronization: a synchronized deletion can remove the file everywhere, while a versioned backup preserves recoverable history. Practice restoring a file or configuration rather than assuming backup exists because a folder is present.
pages.sourceLesson: Retention: computer applications, data, ports, and calculation integrity

pages.title: A computer repeatedly moves, transforms, and stores information
pages.text: The CPU fetches instructions and data, decodes operations, executes them using registers/ALU, and updates state. RAM provides volatile working storage; flash/ROM retains code/data without power; peripherals connect timers, converters, communication, and pins; buses carry address, data, and control. A microcontroller integrates these blocks on one device.
pages.remember: CPU executes; memory stores; peripherals interact; buses connect.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: Computer architecture, CPU blocks, memory, block diagrams, and flowcharts
pages.text: A computer system can be divided into input, processing, memory/storage, communication and output. Inside a processor/microprocessor, the control unit sequences operations, the arithmetic/logic unit performs calculations/logic, registers hold immediate working state, buses/interconnect move addresses/data/control, and clock/reset mechanisms coordinate startup/execution. Cache and memory interfaces reduce the speed gap to external memory. Volatile RAM loses contents without power; nonvolatile flash/ROM retains code/data; mass storage provides longer-term file storage with very different latency/endurance. A computer block diagram shows hardware/data relationships, while a software flowchart shows sequence and decisions. Troubleshooting uses both: “which block should receive this signal/data?” is a block-diagram question; “which branch should execute next?” is a flowchart question.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: Peripherals and interface devices/cards
pages.text: A peripheral is an attached device that extends input, output, storage, sensing or communication capability: keyboards, displays, printers, drives, cameras, USB devices and network adapters are examples. Interface devices/chips/cards bridge electrical/protocol expectations between the CPU/system bus and external equipment. Examples include USB controllers/hubs, UART/serial interfaces, Ethernet/network interface controllers, storage controllers, audio codecs/interfaces, GPIO/I/O expanders and data-acquisition cards. Installing hardware is only part of bring-up: power, connector/pinout, bus enumeration, driver, address/resource configuration and functional test must all agree. An unrecognized peripheral may be a cable/power/port problem, missing driver, unsupported protocol/device class, resource/configuration issue or failed hardware.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: A computer is coordinated storage, processing, and I/O
pages.text: At a high level, a CPU fetches instructions and data from memory, executes operations using registers/ALU/control logic, and communicates with peripherals through buses or mapped interfaces. Volatile memory such as RAM loses contents without power; nonvolatile memory such as flash retains program/data. Storage, working memory, registers, cache, and peripheral registers serve different roles. A block diagram is useful because it shows where information is stored, transformed, and transferred without implying exact physical layout.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: PLCs are computers optimized for industrial control
pages.text: A PLC reads inputs, executes a control program, updates outputs, and performs communications/diagnostics in a repeating scan or platform-specific execution model. Ladder logic uses relay-like contacts and coils; function block and structured text offer other representations. Timers, counters, state, interlocks, and fail-safe design connect software logic to physical I/O. A displayed software bit is not proof that a field voltage or actuator changed; technicians verify both program state and actual terminal behavior.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

pages.title: Garbled data is a useful symptom
pages.text: Consistently wrong characters often suggest baud/clock/format mismatch. Nothing at the MCU TX pin suggests firmware/pin-mux/clock path; correct MCU waveform but nothing at the adapter suggests wiring or level conversion; correct bytes in a terminal but not Python suggests port/encoding/line-handling software. A logic analyzer or scope localizes the boundary.
pages.remember: Observe the signal at each interface before rewriting both ends.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: Errors point to different layers
pages.text: No transitions can mean wrong pin, no firmware output, broken wire, missing ground, or wrong measurement point. Repeating but unreadable patterns can mean wrong baud/framing or voltage-level mismatch. Clean electrical frames with wrong characters can indicate framing/encoding assumptions. Correct bytes reaching the host but wrong application values point to parsing/protocol logic. A logic analyzer decoder is useful only after the raw waveform levels and timing make sense; a decoder setting can hide the real problem by confidently interpreting the wrong baud.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

pages.title: Applications depend on layered computer services
pages.text: The operating system enumerates devices and manages ports/files; a driver connects hardware to OS interfaces; libraries expose APIs; the application frames, parses, evaluates, and stores data. A missing serial port can be cable, power, driver, permissions, enumeration, or application selection. Name the failing layer before reinstalling everything.
pages.remember: Hardware → driver/OS → port/API → framing/parsing → application/test.
pages.sourceLesson: Retention: computer applications, data, ports, and calculation integrity

pages.title: Calculation integrity means estimating before trusting software
pages.text: Spreadsheets and scripts can repeat an error perfectly. Before accepting a calculated result, estimate order of magnitude and use dimensional reasoning. A 3.3 V / 330 ohm result should be about 10 mA, not 10 A. A 1 kHz period should be about 1 ms. When code converts ADC counts to volts, test zero, full-scale, midpoint, and one known input. These boundary checks are simple but catch sign, scale, integer-division, and unit errors quickly.
pages.sourceLesson: Retention: computer applications, data, ports, and calculation integrity

examples.title: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

detail.problem: An 8-bit unsigned counter holding 255 is incremented once.
steps: Eight unsigned bits represent 0 through 255.
255 is binary 11111111.
Adding one produces 1 00000000; only eight stored bits remain.
The stored result wraps to 0 in unsigned arithmetic.
detail.answer: 0, due to modulo-256 unsigned wrap.
detail.transfer: A wrapped timer/counter can break comparisons unless rollover is handled intentionally.

examples.title: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

detail.problem: A small C program compiles each source file successfully but the final build reports 'undefined reference to read_sensor'.
steps: Compilation succeeded, so the syntax in the individual source files is acceptable enough to produce objects.
The undefined reference appears during linking because a required symbol declaration/call exists but the linker cannot find a matching definition in linked objects/libraries.
Check whether the implementation file is included in the build, symbol spelling/signature matches, and the correct library/object is linked.
Do not troubleshoot runtime sensor wiring until an executable image exists.
detail.answer: Treat this as a link-stage dependency/symbol problem, not a runtime hardware failure.
detail.meaning: Identifying the build stage narrows the search space before any code or hardware change.

examples.title: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

detail.problem: At 115200 baud, estimate one bit time and a 10-bit 8N1 character time.
steps: 8N1 commonly has 1 start + 8 data + 1 stop = 10 bits.
Tchar ≈ 86.8 µs.
Maximum ideal character rate is about 11,520 per second before software/protocol overhead.
detail.answer: About 8.68 µs per bit and 86.8 µs per 8N1 character.
detail.transfer: A logic-analyzer cursor can verify baud by measuring bit width.

examples.title: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

detail.problem: A UART uses 115200 baud, 8N1. Estimate bit time and approximate 10-bit frame time for one byte.
steps: 8N1 frame has 1 start + 8 data + 1 stop = 10 bits.
Frame time≈86.8 us per byte, ignoring gaps.
Maximum theoretical byte rate is about 11,520 bytes/s before protocol overhead.
detail.answer: 8.68 us per bit and about 86.8 us per 8N1 byte frame.
detail.meaning: Timing calculations let you choose scope/analyzer time scales and realistic software timeouts.

examples.title: Retention: computer applications, data, ports, and calculation integrity

detail.problem: A test logs 3300 from the device but compares it directly with a 3.2–3.4 V limit.
steps: The device value may be millivolts while limits are volts.
Confirm protocol/schema and unit at source.
Convert 3300 mV to 3.300 V exactly once in a named layer.
Store raw value/unit and converted value/unit; test boundaries.
detail.answer: The raw/limit unit mismatch can create a false fail or pass.
detail.transfer: Explicit units are as important in software tests as in Ohm’s-law work.

guided.text: Classify five failures as compile, link, load/program, or runtime: syntax error, undefined reference, programmer cannot connect, program hard-faults, missing header declaration warning.
Draw CPU, RAM, flash/nonvolatile storage, and peripheral I/O blocks. Trace what happens from power-up to executing an instruction that reads an input.
Explain a PLC scan using a start/stop input and motor output, then identify what field measurement is needed to prove the output actually energized.
Draw an 8N1 frame for data byte 0x55 assuming idle-high and LSB-first. Label start, each data bit, and stop.
A logic analyzer decodes nonsense at 115200 but the raw bit period measures about 104 us. Estimate the actual baud rate and state the likely problem.
List the physical checks before blaming parsing: voltage levels, ground/reference, TX/RX crossover, idle level, actual baud, frame settings.

teachBack: Explain the path from C source file to running executable, then connect that path to CPU, memory, and I/O hardware. Include how a PLC scan differs from assuming software state equals physical output.
Explain an 8N1 UART frame from idle through stop bit, calculate bit time from baud, and describe how you would distinguish wrong baud from wrong voltage/wiring using raw waveform evidence.
Explain how a raw ADC count becomes a trustworthy logged voltage. Include units, scaling, boundary tests, metadata, graph labeling, and why a script's output still needs a sanity check.

questions.prompt: Which check makes a backup more trustworthy?
choices: Restoring a test copy and verifying the files are usable
Renaming the original file without copying it
Keeping the only copy on the failing drive
Deleting version information from all copies
questions.explanation: A backup must be recoverable. A restore test checks that the saved material can actually be used.

questions.prompt: An unexpected message asks for your password to download a board driver. What is the appropriate response?
choices: Verify the source independently and use the manufacturer's trusted download route.
Send the password to make installation faster.
questions.explanation: Source verification reduces phishing and malicious software risk; unsolicited requests are not proof of authenticity.

questions.prompt: A USB instrument is connected but not recognized. What is a useful first software check?
choices: Check the operating system's device status and the correct driver requirements.
questions.explanation: Device status and supported drivers help isolate a host configuration problem before replacing hardware.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a basic networked computer from a stand-alone one?
choices: It can exchange data or access services through network connections.
Its CPU no longer executes instructions.
questions.explanation: Networking adds communication with other devices; it does not replace local computing or access controls.

questions.prompt: Which problem is addressed by surge protection rather than antivirus software?
choices: A transient overvoltage on a power connection
questions.explanation: Electrical transients and malicious software are different risks with different controls.
