glossary.definition: The function or routine executed in response to an interrupt.
glossary.technical: An interrupt service routine handles the interrupt source, performs time-critical work, and returns control to interrupted execution according to the architecture.

sourceDetail.name: Arm Developer Documentation
sourceDetail.note: Processor architecture, register, exception, debug, and embedded-system terminology.

glossary.definition: A two-wire addressed serial bus commonly used for sensors and peripheral ICs.
glossary.technical: The I²C bus uses serial data (SDA) and serial clock (SCL), open-drain/open-collector signaling, pull-up resistors, addressing, and acknowledge cycles.

sourceDetail.name: NXP — UM10204 I²C-bus Specification and User Manual
sourceDetail.note: Original I²C bus specification maintained by NXP.

glossary.definition: A junction field-effect transistor controlled by a reverse-biased gate junction.
glossary.technical: A JFET uses an electric field from a PN-junction gate to vary channel conductivity and normally draws very little gate current.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: The SI unit used to measure energy or work.
glossary.technical: One joule is one newton-metre; electrically, one volt across one coulomb corresponds to one joule of energy transfer.

sourceDetail.name: NIST — SI Units: Electric Current and Electrical Derived Units
sourceDetail.note: U.S. national metrology reference for SI electrical quantities and units.

glossary.definition: A structured text format for representing objects, arrays, numbers, strings, booleans, and null values.
glossary.technical: JavaScript Object Notation is a language-independent data-interchange syntax commonly used for configuration, APIs, logs, and structured test results.

sourceDetail.name: NIST CSRC Glossary
sourceDetail.note: NIST technical terminology for computing, firmware, hardware, and related systems.

glossary.definition: A standardized test/debug interface used for boundary scan and processor/system debugging.
glossary.technical: JTAG commonly refers to IEEE 1149.1 test-access architecture using a test access port and instruction/data registers; many devices extend it for debug.

sourceDetail.name: Arm Developer Documentation
sourceDetail.note: Processor architecture, register, exception, debug, and embedded-system terminology.

glossary.definition: A point where conductors, device regions, or circuit paths meet.
glossary.technical: In circuit work a junction is a connection point between multiple conductive paths; in semiconductor work it can mean the interface between differently doped regions.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: The temperature of the active semiconductor junction inside a device.
glossary.technical: Junction temperature Tj is estimated from ambient or case temperature, dissipated power, and the applicable thermal resistance/impedance network.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: The rule that current flowing into a node must balance current flowing out.
glossary.technical: Kirchhoff’s Current Law expresses conservation of charge at a circuit node: the algebraic sum of branch currents at a node is zero.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: The SI prefix meaning one thousand times the base unit.
glossary.technical: kilo, symbol k, represents a factor of 10³.

sourceDetail.name: NIST — SI Units: Electric Current and Electrical Derived Units
sourceDetail.note: U.S. national metrology reference for SI electrical quantities and units.

glossary.definition: Two basic circuit laws relating currents at nodes and voltages around loops.
glossary.technical: Kirchhoff’s Current Law follows charge conservation at a node, while Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law follows conservation of energy around a closed loop.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A component, signal, configuration, or unit already verified to operate correctly.
glossary.technical: A known-good reference is used for substitution or comparison to separate DUT behavior from setup, tool, or configuration problems.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: The rule that voltage rises and drops around a closed loop must balance.
glossary.technical: Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law states that the algebraic sum of voltages around a closed loop is zero for the lumped-circuit model.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A storage element that can hold one bit of state and is typically level-sensitive.
glossary.technical: A latch is a bistable storage circuit whose state can change while an enable condition is active.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: An instrument used to measure inductance, capacitance, resistance, and often related impedance parameters.
glossary.technical: An LCR meter applies an AC stimulus and derives impedance-related component values at specified test conditions.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A linear regulator designed to regulate with a relatively small input-to-output voltage difference.
glossary.technical: A low-dropout regulator maintains regulation down to a specified dropout voltage that is lower than conventional linear-regulator requirements.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A light-dependent resistor whose resistance changes with illumination.
glossary.technical: An LDR, or photoresistor, is a photoconductive device whose resistance generally decreases as incident light increases.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A diode that emits light when current flows in the forward direction.
glossary.technical: A light-emitting diode converts electrical carrier recombination energy into optical radiation.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A low-cost single-wire serial network used for simple distributed embedded nodes, especially in vehicles.
glossary.technical: Local Interconnect Network is a master-scheduled serial bus with defined frame timing, identifiers, checksums, and a single-wire physical layer.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: How much a regulated output changes when input voltage changes.
glossary.technical: Line regulation specifies output-voltage variation versus input-voltage variation under stated load and temperature conditions.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: An operating region where a device behaves approximately linearly for the intended use.
glossary.technical: For MOSFET terminology, linear or triode operation occurs when the channel behaves resistively; datasheet wording should be checked because “linear region” can also describe analog operation more broadly.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A regulator that controls output voltage by operating a pass device in its linear region.
glossary.technical: A linear regulator dissipates excess voltage as heat to maintain a controlled output, subject to dropout and thermal limits.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A build tool that combines compiled code and data into an executable image.
glossary.technical: The linker resolves symbols, places sections according to a linker script or memory map, and emits the final program image.

sourceDetail.name: Arm Developer Documentation
sourceDetail.note: Processor architecture, register, exception, debug, and embedded-system terminology.

glossary.definition: How much a regulated output changes as load current changes.
glossary.technical: Load regulation specifies output-voltage variation between stated load conditions with other conditions held within the specification.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: The effective resistance presented by the circuit or device receiving power or signal energy.
glossary.technical: Load resistance is the resistive component of the impedance connected to a source or driving network.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A change in the circuit being measured caused by the measuring instrument itself.
glossary.technical: Instrument input impedance, capacitance, probe characteristics, or current burden can alter the measurand when connected.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: Recording events, measurements, status, or diagnostic information during program execution or testing.
glossary.technical: Technical logging captures timestamped, structured evidence that supports debugging, traceability, trend analysis, and test reproducibility.

sourceDetail.name: Python 3 Documentation
sourceDetail.note: Language-authoritative Python terminology.

glossary.definition: The binary LOW state represented by a voltage within the device’s valid low-level range.
glossary.technical: Logic 0 is a symbolic state; the acceptable electrical voltage range is defined by input/output low-level specifications such as VIL and VOL.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: The binary HIGH state represented by a voltage within the device’s valid high-level range.
glossary.technical: Logic 1 is a symbolic state; the acceptable electrical voltage range is defined by specifications such as VIH and VOH.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: An instrument that captures and displays multiple digital signals so their timing and protocol relationships can be inspected.
glossary.technical: A logic analyzer samples digital channels and represents logic states versus time; many models also decode serial protocols.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A group of digital devices built with compatible circuit technology and electrical conventions.
glossary.technical: Logic families such as CMOS or TTL define supply ranges, thresholds, drive characteristics, speed, and power behavior.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A circuit that performs a basic Boolean operation on one or more binary inputs.
glossary.technical: Logic gates implement Boolean functions and produce output logic levels based on defined input-state combinations.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: The digital HIGH state represented by a voltage within a device’s valid high-level range.
glossary.technical: Logic HIGH corresponds to a valid logic-1 electrical level defined by output-high and input-high specifications, not necessarily exactly the supply voltage.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)
sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

glossary.definition: A voltage range interpreted as a digital 0 or digital 1.
glossary.technical: Digital interfaces specify acceptable input and guaranteed output voltage ranges rather than one exact voltage for each state.

sourceDetail.name: IEC Electropedia — International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEC 60050)

sourceDetail.note: International electrotechnical terminology maintained by the IEC.

sourceDetail.note: Industry standards for PCB, soldering, rework, and cable/harness workmanship.
